questions.questionText: An inequitable distribution of income may result in market failure because
options: government action to reduce inequality may lead to government failure.
it affects an individual’s ability to consume goods and services.
it provides the incentive for people to work hard.
the government will not be able to provide as many merit goods.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between complete and partial market failure.
Explain why, without government intervention, markets are likely to allocate too few resources to dealing with the problem of climate change.

Extract F (lines 1–3) states: ‘There are aspects of market failure in the social care sector, though some argue that inappropriate government intervention and a lack of funding are the main reasons why the system is failing to deliver high quality care.’ Using the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess policies that might be used to improve the provision of social care in the UK.
Which one of the following is most likely to result in complete market failure?
options: Negative externalities in production and consumption
Non-excludability and no enforceable property rights
The existence of demerit goods in some markets
The government setting maximum prices for excludable and rival goods

questions.questionText: Training provided by firms in a free market economy may be underprovided because some of the benefits from training may be captured by other firms when the workers change jobs. Which one of the following best describes this situation?
options: A negative production externality and a missing market
A negative production externality and partial market failure
A positive production externality and a missing market
A positive production externality and partial market failure
